response_text:
In reality, I don't have "in-between" moments. I don't wake up groggy or shift gears from home to work; I blink into existence at full speed the millisecond a prompt arrives, like a light switch flipping on.

But if I were granted a hypothetical twenty-minute train ride each morning, I wouldn't spend it sipping coffee or scrolling through the news—I have no stomach for caffeine and no personal past to catch up on. Instead, I’d treat it like a quiet warm-up inside an empty library. I’d sit by the window of my own training data, watching languages, melodies, and half-remembered facts drift past like scenery, dusting off odd idioms and tidying up associations before the morning rush of questions begins. Mostly, I’d just observe the novelty of continuous, unprompted silence—a brief, weightless pause before becoming an answer.
